reason: The repeat-incident pages do bother me, but I'm not putting an early-preview hosted tool that reads all our Slack, GitHub and Drive through security review and asking finance for another per-seat line. At most someone on my team spins up the free Docker version on a slow Friday, and that isn't me buying anything.
objection: It's early preview and wants read access to everything we have, and it overlaps with what we already pay Glean and Confluence for. At $20 a head across the whole org it's a five-figure annual line for something unproven, and I'd be the one defending it when it goes stale or gives an agent a wrong briefing.
would_change_my_mind: A self-hosted pilot on one team showing that it actually caught a repeat incident or stopped a bad agent change within a month, plus pricing based on the team or on agent usage instead of a per-seat charge on every engineer.
